text:
Nina (Marketing): Quick kickoff—we need a fresh battlecard and inbound-routing plan tied to the webinar + benchmark post. Output: AE one-pager, SDR pocket-card (3 lines), and HubSpot mapping that prioritizes high-cost risk deals.
Theo (Product): Agree. Callouts to prove: consistent p95 under burst, identical API surface across modes, and operational levers (batching, prefix cache, quant profiles). I'll export microbench snapshots.
Carlos (Sales): SDR pocket lines (very short):
- "Do you know what your inference bill looks like at scale?"
- "We make serving predictable across cloud, dedicated, and private."
- Rebuttal vs managed cloud: "Managed APIs hide serving risk until you hit production."
I'll craft a startup + enterprise variant.
Rina (Growth): Routing idea: use a 3-factor lead score (est_tokens, company_arr, role_weight). Pseudocode to hand to ops: 
```
score = norm(est_monthly_tokens) * 0.6 + norm(company.ARR) * 0.3 + (role == 'engineer' ? 0.1 : 0)
if (score >= 0.8) route='enterprise-AE'
else if (score >= 0.4) route='tech-demo-webinar'
else route='nurture-marketing'
```
We'll capture est_tokens as a hidden field and normalize on capture.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for webinar infra set Thu 09:00 PT. CI: https://ci.redwood/deploy/824 (green).
Nina (Marketing): Webinar narrative notes: 6m market context, 12m benchmark story (customer cost curve + p95 chart), 18m live demo showing fallback orchestration (hosted -> dedicated -> lite-quant), 9m Q&A. Slide headline: "When serving is the product."
Theo (Product): Microbench plan: compare ModelQ across CloudAPI_A (managed), self-host baseline, Redwood-hosted, and Redwood-dedicated. Metrics: cold-start p95, steady-state p95 at 750 concurrent sessions, and tokens_per_USD. I will include hardware, batch policy, and quant caveats.
Carlos (Sales): AE one-liners for slide: "Predictable serving, predictable cost." and "Ship product features, not ops runbooks." Prefer the first for executive decks.
Rina (Growth): CTA experiments: "Join the benchmark" vs "Get a cost estimate". For score >= 0.8 surface an AE calendar slot in the confirmation email and flag in CRM.
Nina (Marketing): Competitive soundbite to test vs cloud APIs: "Cloud APIs get you a model. Redwood gets your product to market without surprise serving bills." Keep it tight.
Theo (Product): Include a short methodology blurb in the battlecard: dataset, seq_len, batch policy, quant profile, and orchestration chain. Also show a tiny example table: [env, seq_len, p95_ms, tokens_per_USD].
Carlos (Sales): Procurement-friendly bullets for the battlecard (2 lines each): pricing (usage + reserved), SLA tiers (Hosted / Dedicated), data residency & private control plane. I'll keep them concise.
Rina (Growth): I'll own the HubSpot mapping doc and a short test plan (capture hidden est_tokens, run A/B CTAs, escalate score>=0.8 to AE). Will share mapping link when ready.
Nina (Marketing): Owners & deadlines: Theo -> battlecard content + CSVs; Carlos -> SDR pocket + procurement bullets; Rina -> routing + CTA tests; Nina -> webinar script & slides. Drafts by Mon EOD.
Theo (Product): One more competitive angle vs infra vendors: emphasize compilation/kernel tuning and orchestration—the vendor provides optimized runtime choices out of box. Short line included.
Carlos (Sales): I'll prepare 3 1-line rebuttals vs self-host: ops overhead, long tail performance tuning, and hidden run costs.
Nina (Marketing): Great. I'll synthesize into a single-page PDF and a 2-line social snippet for the blog push. Post drafts here. :rocket:
